lesson.title: Percentages
lesson.body:
Building blocks. 10% = move the decimal point; 1% = move it twice. Everything else is built from these: 17% of 340 → 10% = 34, 1% = 3.4, 7% = 23.8 → 57.8. 5% = half of 10%; 15% = 10% + 5%; 25% = ÷ 4; 12.5% = ÷ 8; 92% = 100% − 8%.

Swap trick: x% of y = y% of x. 18% of 50 = 50% of 18 = 9. 4% of 75 = 75% of 4 = 3.

Percent change = change ÷ starting value. 80 → 92: +12 / 80 = 0.15 → +15%. Always divide by where you started. Quick estimate: find 1% of the start (0.8) and ask how many of those fit in the change.

Successive changes multiply. +20% then −15%: 1.2 × 0.85 = 1.02 → +2%, not +5%. Shortcut: a + b + ab/100 = 20 − 15 − 3 = 2. (+10% then −10% is −1%.)

Reverse percent divides. "After a 25% increase it's 150": 150 = 1.25 × x, so x = 150 ÷ 1.25 = 150 × 4/5 = 120. Subtracting 25% of 150 (giving 112.5) is the classic mistake. Know the fraction forms: 1.25 = 5/4, 1.2 = 6/5, 0.8 = 4/5, 0.75 = 3/4, 1.125 = 9/8, 0.875 = 7/8.
